title: Boss: the leaky bank account
summary: Seal up a bank account that anyone can corrupt.

steps.title: The leak
body: `Account` exposes a public `List<decimal> Transactions`, a settable `Balance`, a `bool IsFrozen` that nothing checks, and amounts as raw `decimal` that can be negative. Callers reach in and edit everything.
You will fix it in three moves: a value object for amounts, an account that guards its own state, and a frozen state that cannot be ignored.

steps.title: A value for amounts
prompt: - has a constructor `Amount(decimal value)` throwing `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` unless `value > 0`
- has `override string ToString()` returning the value with 2 decimals (`12.50`)
template: Dojo.Eq("equal by value", new Amount(5m), new Amount(5m));

steps.title: An account that guards itself
prompt: `Amount` is given. Rewrite `Account` so nobody can corrupt it:
- `IReadOnlyList<decimal> History` (deposits positive, withdrawals negative) backed by a private list
- `void Deposit(Amount a)` and `bool Withdraw(Amount a)` (returns `false` and changes nothing when funds are short)
Callers must not be able to set the balance or add to the history.
starter: public Amount(decimal value) => Value = value > 0 ? value : throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(value));
solution: public Amount(decimal value) => Value = value > 0 ? value : throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(value));
public decimal Balance { get; private set; }
template: Dojo.Check("Balance cannot be set from outside", typeof(Account).GetProperty("Balance")!.SetMethod?.IsPublic != true, "Balance has a public setter");
Dojo.Check("History is read-only", dojoAcc.History is not List<decimal>, "History is a List callers could cast and modify");
hints: Keep a `private readonly List<decimal> _history` and expose `_history.AsReadOnly()`.
`Withdraw` starts with a guard: `if (a.Value > Balance) return false;`

steps.title: Frozen means frozen
prompt: The bank can freeze accounts. Instead of a `bool IsFrozen` that methods might forget to check, model the account's state:
- `abstract record AccountState;` with `record Open(decimal Balance) : AccountState;` and `record Frozen(decimal Balance, string Reason) : AccountState;`
- `static AccountState Withdraw(AccountState s, decimal amount)` returns a new `Open` with less money; a `Frozen` account, or not enough money, throws `InvalidOperationException`
- `static AccountState Freeze(AccountState s, string reason)` turns an `Open` into `Frozen` with the same balance
starter: public void Withdraw(decimal amount) => Balance -= amount;
solution: record Frozen(decimal Balance, string Reason) : AccountState;
public static AccountState Withdraw(AccountState s, decimal amount) => s switch
Open o when amount <= o.Balance => o with { Balance = o.Balance - amount },
Frozen f => throw new InvalidOperationException("frozen: " + f.Reason),
public static AccountState Freeze(AccountState s, string reason) => s switch
template: Dojo.Eq("withdraw from open", new Open(30m) as AccountState, dojoS);
Dojo.Eq("freeze keeps the balance", new Frozen(30m, "fraud check") as AccountState, dojoF);
